title: Kuchh Adab ke Baare Mein, part 2

paras.en: These questions are necessary and important for every student of literature who wants to think about and understand literature and form some correct opinion about it. Without fully fixing these questions in mind, literature cannot be fully understood. So it is a result of their importance that along with literature, students of literature in every age have also been pondering over these questions, and according to their respective abilities have thrown light on them in various ways and from various angles.

paras.en: Yes! So we have to see why and for what purpose literature came into being. The antiquity of literature can be judged from just one thing about it: that from the time man was newly come into this world, from that very time he began the creation of literature. The essence of creation and the desire for creation are quite natural within man; so man feels pleasure not only in the creation of literature but of everything: the creation of something that is used in everyday life, from which humanity gets ease and comfort, or the creation of something from which merely by looking at it he gets pleasure, delight and joy. This is the result of that natural desire for creation which has been deposited in man by nature. In exactly the same way is the creation of literature, in which this same natural desire of man has a part. Its nature, however, changes somewhat. The other creations relate to materiality, but matter has no part in the creation of literature; on the contrary its nature is spiritual. To clothe in the garment of beautiful words the waves that keep rising in man’s emotions and feelings is called literature. Obviously man is a puppet of emotions, and at the beginning of creation he was nothing but emotions. In those days the elements of intellect and awareness had not fully awakened in him. He could think and understand little about things. External things and the slightest events arising from them worked like a wind on the still sea of his emotions, from which a state of tide, ebb and turbulence arose in it. These turbulent waves of the sea of emotions he used to give the form of words, which we today are compelled to count under literature.
